title: Calendar/Rebalance Daily Proxy
purpose: Create a small auditable daily event calendar for month-end, quarter-end, and options-expiration windows before testing calendar or rebalance pressure hypotheses.
data_grain: daily event calendar joined to daily OHLCV returns
candidate_sources: exchange trading calendars for market holidays and trading days
OCC or exchange options-expiration calendars for standard monthly expiration dates
index or fund methodology documents for documented rebalance timing
manual deterministic calendar generation for month-end and quarter-end labels
construction_rules: Define event windows before joining any return data.
Generate month-end and quarter-end events from trading calendars, not from price behavior.
Use standard third-Friday monthly options expiration only if the date is verified against an exchange/OCC calendar.
Version the generated calendar and preserve source notes for every event type.
Do not add or remove event windows after inspecting strategy returns.
quality_checks: Every event_date, window_start, and window_end must be a valid trading day for the tested symbol universe.
Every row must include source_name and source_url_or_note.
generated_without_return_data must be true for every row.
The calendar must cover the full tested price-data date range or explicitly state coverage gaps.
minimum_viable_tests: Event-study summary of SPY, QQQ, IWM, and TLT returns around month-end and quarter-end windows versus non-event windows.
A no-trade diagnostic report before any executable strategy is created.
A single prespecified long/cash or exposure-adjustment proxy only after the event-study summary identifies a plausible direction.
known_limitations: Daily data may miss intraday effects around close, open, or expiration settlement.
Simple month-end and quarter-end labels are a crude proxy for actual institutional flow.
Options-expiration mechanics may require intraday data or options data before becoming economically meaningful.
The first generated file only includes month-end and quarter-end proxy windows, not options-expiration, index-rebalance, or fund-flow events.
The generated file uses SPY trading dates as a practical daily calendar proxy rather than a dedicated exchange-calendar package.
next_action: Inspect the generated event rows, then build a no-trade event-study summary before creating any executable calendar strategy.
